**Identity** is what a thing is for someone, not what it is in itself. Take everything the reading connects to a thing (what it touches, what happens around it, how that changes over time) and cut it off where the difference stops mattering. That cut-out neighborhood, seen from a particular perspective, is its identity. Two names are the same thing when their neighborhoods match under that cut, and when swapping one out for a generic stand-in disturbs the surroundings in the same way, by more than chance would. That is why identity is relative (it depends on the for-whom), revisable (more reading can move it), and earned (the thing has to carry weight, so idle things never count as the same).

**A definition** is that same fold written down in a portable phrase, by someone, so it can be carried and reused. "Faction" on its own is just a word, and Madison's sentence compresses what he wants it to mean into something that can travel. Because it is compressed, the phrase can't replace the word, which is why my substitution test failed. What it does is shift the odds: once a word is defined, some later uses become much more likely and others much less. It governs by changing probabilities, not by laying down a rule. The giver is the for-whom, so a definition is only as authoritative as its giver. HUD's definition of affordability governs HUD's usage, and a planning document borrowing it may use the word differently.

So the two are one thing seen from two ends. Identity is the fold found by reading, and a definition is the fold stated in advance. A definition succeeds when what you find matches what was stated, and it drifts when the reading moves away from the stated fold.

Three things are not established. The identity definition is still a nomination in the code, with its measurements pending. The claim that a definition is a prior on usage is untested, and the Federalist result is only suggestive support. And I have not yet shown that a definition predicts anything beyond its own words, which is the control I proposed.

# eo-compendium

A document archive, not a code repo. This exists so that the papers built on
`eoreader6`'s null-first measurement engine, its evidence kernel, and The
Fold have a single, stable place to cite — one that survives a source repo
being renamed, repurposed, or force-pushed over, because every file here is
a **copy**, stamped in [PROVENANCE.md](PROVENANCE.md) with exactly which
repo and commit it came from and when it was copied.

It exists because of a real incident: `eoreader6.1`'s history was rewritten
to start at a "published snapshot" commit, and the evidence kernel material
(`kernel.eot`, `KERNEL.md`, `PARITY.md`) briefly looked like it had vanished.
It hadn't — it was public the whole time, just under a different repo name
(`eoreader6-kernel-rebuild-2026-08`) that nothing had cited by name. This
compendium is the fix: pin the documents themselves, not just a URL that
assumes a repo keeps meaning the same thing forever.

## Scope

The full EOReader → chat-app → Fold lineage (`eoReader` through `the-fold`),
the constitution that governs it, and the evidence/assay discipline the
null-first measurement work is built on. It does not attempt to cover every
`eo-*` repo in the account — see
[REPO-MAP.md](evidence-discipline/eo-evidence/REPO-MAP.md) for a wider map
if that's ever needed.

**Legacy vs. active.** Everything through `eoreader6`, plus `eochat`,
`eoWebLLM`, `eochatX`, and `eoreader6-kernel-rebuild-2026-08`, is finished,
dormant work — ported once, frozen on purpose. `eo-constitution`,

# EO Wiki — GitHub-native storage (the NPJ method)

The wiki has no application backend. All data lives natively in this GitHub
repo; writes go **browser → n8n webhook → GitHub Contents API**, the same
pattern the NPJ site uses.

## How it works

- **Storage.** Every article is a plain Markdown file in this repo under
  `articles/<type>/<slug>.md`, plus a manifest at `articles/index.json` that the
  app reads on load. Site-level data lives under `site/`:
  - `site/getstarted.json` — the "Get started" operator-card assignments
    (curated by the admin, seen by every visitor).
  - `site/auth.json` — SHA-256 hashes of the admin publish key(s); this is what
    the webhook authorizes against (hashes only, never the key).
  The site is served by GitHub Pages (`experientialontology.org`), so reads are
  same-origin static fetches — no server, no API tokens, no rate limits.
- **Reading.** `index.html` fetches `articles/index.json`, then loads each
  article file and renders its Markdown body with `marked`. It also fetches
  `site/getstarted.json` for the front-page cards.
- **Full Markdown export (permanent URL).** The entire wiki, unabridged, is
  always available as a single Markdown file at
  **<https://experientialontology.org/eo-wiki.md>**. It is byte-for-byte the
  in-app "Download all as Markdown" output (every article, title-ordered, joined
  with `\n\n---\n\n---\n\n`). See "Full Markdown export" below.
- **Editing (admin only).** Sign in with the editor password. On save, the app
  POSTs the changed file(s) as JSON to the **n8n publish webhook** with
  `Authorization: Bearer <admin key>`. The workflow verifies the caller
  **server-side** — it SHA-256-hashes the Bearer key and only commits when the
  hash appears in the `admins` list of the committed `site/auth.json` — then
  writes the file to this repo on `main` via the GitHub Contents API. GitHub
  Pages redeploys and the change goes live.
- **The endpoint is not a secret.** Because authorization is enforced in the
  workflow (the NPJ method), the webhook URL sits in plain text in
  `index.html` (`DEFAULT_PUBLISH_ENDPOINT`). It can be overridden per-browser
  via `localStorage['eo_publish_cfg_v1'] = '{"endpoint":"https://…"}'`.
  This replaces the old scheme where the URL was AES-GCM encrypted in source
  (`WEBHOOK_ENC`) and the unauthenticated webhook URL itself was the write
  capability.
- **Login** uses the same password as before. Its SHA-256 is in `ADMIN_HASH`
  (client-side UX check) and in `site/auth.json` (the server-side gate); the
  password itself is never stored in the repo.

## What an admin can do

Create, edit (Markdown), search-and-replace, and bulk-edit articles, assign
"Get started" operator cards, and download a full Markdown export. Each write
publishes the affected file through the webhook: articles publish
`articles/<type>/<slug>.md` and refresh `articles/index.json`; card
assignments publish `site/getstarted.json` (debounced into one commit).

### Client publish behavior (mirrors NPJ)

- Requests are bounded by an `AbortController` (120 s).
- The **response body, not the HTTP status, is the verdict**: the workflow
  answers `{ ok, gh_status, commit_sha, bytes, error }` even on failure. A
  structured `{ ok:false }` fails fast; only body-less gateway blips
  (408/429/502/503/504) and GitHub 409/422 blob-SHA races are retried, with
  backoff 600 ms → 1.5 s → 3 s.

## Full Markdown export

The whole wiki, unabridged, lives at one stable URL:

```
https://experientialontology.org/eo-wiki.md
```

`eo-wiki.md` (repo root) is a static file served by GitHub Pages, so the URL is
permanent — fetch it with `curl`, point an LLM at it, or open it in a browser.

- **Build.** `tools/build-full-md.js` reads `articles/index.json`, concatenates
  every article (title-ordered, `site:*` records dropped, joined with
  `\n\n---\n\n---\n\n`) and writes `eo-wiki.md`. The output is byte-for-byte the
  in-app "Download all as Markdown" button. Run manually with
  `node tools/build-full-md.js`.
- **Stays current automatically.** `.github/workflows/build-full-md.yml` reruns
  the build on every push to `main` that touches `articles/**` (i.e. every n8n
  publish) and commits the refreshed `eo-wiki.md`. That commit only touches
  `eo-wiki.md`, never `articles/**`, so it does not retrigger itself. The
  workflow can also be run on demand from the Actions tab (`workflow_dispatch`).

## n8n workflow

Import `tools/n8n-publish-eo-wiki.workflow.json` (replaces the old
`n8n-publish-wiki.workflow.json`). Node flow, modeled on NPJ's `publish-npj`:

```
Publish Webhook → Extract Token → Hash Token → Fetch Auth → Authorize → Authorized?
  ├─ no  → Respond Unauthorized (401)
  └─ yes → GH Get File → Build Content → Delete?
             ├─ yes → GH Delete
             └─ no  → Exists? → GH Update / GH Create
           → Check GH Result → Publish OK ({ ok, gh_status, commit_sha, … })
```

The Bearer key is hashed by the built-in **Crypto node** (`Hash Token`), so no
Code node uses `require()` — the workflow runs even on n8n instances where
`NODE_FUNCTION_ALLOW_BUILTIN` is unset.

- **Fetch Auth** reads `site/auth.json` from
  `raw.githubusercontent.com/clovenbradshaw-ctrl/eo-wiki/main` (cache-busted),
  so authorization data lives in the repo itself — no secrets in the workflow.
- **Authorize** SHA-256-hashes the Bearer key and requires the hash to be in
  `admins`, the filename to match the allowlist
  (`articles/<type>/<slug>.md`, `articles/index.json`, `site/*.json`,
  `eo-wiki.md`) and the mode to be `overwrite`, `append` or `delete`.
- **GH Update / GH Create / GH Delete** commit to `clovenbradshaw-ctrl/eo-wiki`
  on `main` with the GitHub OAuth2 credential. `delete` mode removes a file —
  the old webhook couldn't, which is why renames used to leave orphans.
- **Check GH Result** normalizes n8n's varying error shapes and reports success
  only when a commit SHA came back; **Publish OK** returns that verdict as the
  response body with the computed HTTP status and `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`.

After import: re-bind the **GitHub OAuth2 credential** (credential IDs don't
transfer between n8n instances; it needs Contents write on
`clovenbradshaw-ctrl/eo-wiki`), activate the workflow, and deactivate/delete
the old `site/publish-wiki` workflow — it is unauthenticated and its URL is a
write capability.

### Publish request contract

```
POST https://<your-n8n-host>/webhook/site/publish-eo-wiki
Content-Type: application/json
Authorization: Bearer <admin key>
{ "filename": "articles/wiki/emanon.md", "mode": "overwrite",
  "contentRaw": "<file text>", "message": "edit wiki:emanon" }
```

Response: `{ ok, statusCode, filename, mode, bytes, commit_sha, gh_status, error }`.
`mode` may be `overwrite` (replace/create), `append`, or `delete`.

*For most of its life EO was a framework with an anecdote for evidence. The **EO Reader** (`eoreader`, current line 4.2, "the holonic refactor") is the framework running as software: a document-reading and research instrument whose every faculty is an EO contract, and whose behavior can be cited module by module. This article is the map. The two companion articles — [Signal from Noise](/signal-from-noise) and [The Evidence](/the-evidence) — are the parts that matter most for grounding EO's claims about meaning.*

*Citations below are paths into the `eoreader4.2` source tree. They are references, not hyperlinks — the point is that each claim in this article resolves to code you can open.*

---

## The one fact

> The append-only event log is the source of truth. Everything you see is a recomputed **projection** of it. (`README.md`; `src/core/log.js`, `src/core/project.js`)

There is no wall-clock and no mutable store of record. Every event in the log is one of the nine operators, addressed as `operator(Site, Resolution)` at read time. Re-projecting the same log is byte-identical; a retraction is a `SEG` event, never an erasure; nothing derived is ever persisted — the graph, spans, and mentions are always rebuilt by replay (`src/persist/`). This is [The Integral Model](/the-integral-model) made concrete: state as the integral of a typed-transformation log.

## The Problem: What Makes Something This Thing?

What makes an entity *this entity* and not some other? What persists through change? What makes the oak tree that lost its leaves the same oak tree that will grow new ones? What makes the person who woke up this morning the same person who went to sleep last night?

Two answers recur across every domain that has asked the question:

**State identity.** The entity is its current properties. Identity = snapshot. Two objects with identical properties are the same object — or at minimum, interchangeable. This is the default in classical physics (two electrons with the same quantum numbers in the same orbital are interchangeable), in classical logic (Leibniz's identity of indiscernibles), and in most information systems (a database row is its current field values; copy the values, copy the entity).

**Log identity.** The entity is its history. Identity = trajectory. Two objects can have identical current properties and still be different objects if they arrived there by different paths. The entity is constituted by everything that has happened to it — not described by it, but *made of* it. The history is not metadata about the entity. The history is the entity.

EO commits to log identity. This commitment is not a design preference. It is a structural consequence of three features of the architecture: the Given-Log, the INS operator, and Rule 3 (Ineliminability). And it produces a constraint that, independently and for independent reasons, also appears in quantum mechanics: the impossibility of cloning.

# Identity and Definition: One Fold, Two Ends

**Record ID:** wiki:identity-and-definition  
**DB ID:** 81  
**Tags:** 301  
**Keywords:** identity, definition, fold, for-whom, perspective, prior, neighborhood  
**Status:** published  
**Updated:** 2026-10-06T00:00:00.000Z  

---

**Identity** is what a thing is for someone, not what it is in itself. Take everything the reading connects to a thing (what it touches, what happens around it, how that changes over time) and cut it off where the difference stops mattering. That cut-out neighborhood, seen from a particular perspective, is its identity. Two names are the same thing when their neighborhoods match under that cut, and when swapping one out for a generic stand-in disturbs the surroundings in the same way, by more than chance would. That is why identity is relative (it depends on the for-whom), revisable (more reading can move it), and earned (the thing has to carry weight, so idle things never count as the same).

**A definition** is that same fold written down in a portable phrase, by someone, so it can be carried and reused. "Faction" on its own is just a word, and Madison's sentence compresses what he wants it to mean into something that can travel. Because it is compressed, the phrase can't replace the word, which is why my substitution test failed. What it does is shift the odds: once a word is defined, some later uses become much more likely and others much less. It governs by changing probabilities, not by laying down a rule. The giver is the for-whom, so a definition is only as authoritative as its giver. HUD's definition of affordability governs HUD's usage, and a planning document borrowing it may use the word differently.

So the two are one thing seen from two ends. Identity is the fold found by reading, and a definition is the fold stated in advance. A definition succeeds when what you find matches what was stated, and it drifts when the reading moves away from the stated fold.

Three things are not established. The identity definition is still a nomination in the code, with its measurements pending. The claim that a definition is a prior on usage is untested, and the Federalist result is only suggestive support. And I have not yet shown that a definition predicts anything beyond its own words, which is the control I proposed.

---

**EO** proposes nine **transformation operators** — atomic kinds of change that, in combination, are claimed to be sufficient to describe any transformation in any domain. They are organized into a 3⤫3 lattice: three triads (Existence, Structure, Significance) crossed with three modes (Differentiating, Relating, Generating), each instantiating a ground/figure/pattern role.

The operators are best understood not as steps in a process but as **capacities** — things a system becomes able to do. The helix ordering (NUL → SIG → INS → SEG → CON → SYN → DEF → EVA → REC) is the order in which these capacities become available. Each capacity presupposes the ones before it: you cannot draw a distinction without the prior capacity for non-action; you cannot connect without the prior capacity to draw boundaries. The helix is a dependency of enablement, not a recipe you execute.

Within each triad, the three operators are co-constitutive — they co-arise as aspects of a single transformation event. The ordering within a triad is one of logical presupposition, not temporal sequence. Between triads, the dependency is strict: Existence capacities must be available before Structure capacities, which must be available before Significance capacities.

---

## The operators and the capacity ground

The nine operators are one of three projections of EO's 3⤫3⤫3 phase-space capacity ground. The capacity ground has three axes — **Mode** (Differentiating / Relating / Generating), **Domain** (Existence / Structure / Significance), and **Object** (Ground / Figure / Pattern) — producing 27 cells. Projecting onto two axes at a time yields three 3⤫3 faces, each answering a different question:

- **The Act face** (Mode ⤫ Domain): produces the nine operators. Asks *what transformation is happening.*
- **The Site face** (Domain ⤫ Object): produces nine terrain types (Void, Entity, Kind, Field, Link, Network, Atmosphere, Lens, Paradigm). Asks *where in reality is the target.*
- **The Stance face** (Mode ⤫ Object): produces nine stances (Clearing, Dissecting, Binding, Forging, etc.). Asks *at what grain are you engaging.*

The operators are **acts,** not locations. They name what a system *does* at a junction in a pipeline of transformations. The sites name the *terrain* where those acts occur. The resolutions name the *stance* the actor takes. The three faces are complementary projections of the same 27-cell structure. The operator alone tells you the what. The site tells you the where. The resolution tells you the how. All three together — captured in the three-face notation operator(Site, Resolution) — fully encode the capacity ground's three dimensions.

result: {"stdout":"######## the-two-doors

*The deepest invariant in the [EO Reader](/the-eo-reader), and the one the older wiki never named. Every event enters the log through one of two doors, and which door it came through is a fact about the event that can never be forged.*

---

## The law

- **Perceiver door — exafference.** The witnessed world: a source read from disk, a page fetched, a sentence the user typed. `canWitness === true`. It can ground a claim.
- **Enactor door — reafference.** The system's own output: a reflection, a murmur, an inferred connection, a generated paragraph, a code-organ finding. `canWitness === false` — **by type, not by flag** (`src/core/provenance.js`).

"Reafference" is borrowed from biology: the sensory consequences of your own action, which the nervous system must distinguish from sensation caused by the world, or it cannot tell perception from prediction. *You cannot tickle yourself.* The reader enforces the same distinction structurally: a piece of the system's own reasoning can never be laundered into evidence for itself, because `canWitness` is a property of the door it came through, not a boolean anyone can set.

## Why it is a *type*, not a flag

A flag can be flipped; a type cannot be argued with. Because me-ness is constitutive rather than annotated, the firewall is preserved by *composition* — the whole nest of idle cognition ([deep reading](/deep-reading), metacognition, cross-connections) can run unattended and none of it can enter the witnessed record, without the firewall being re-checked at each level. The monologue audit confirms this empirically: strip everything tagged as inference, re-project the graph, and the depicted facts are identical — `factsAdded: 0` across every run (`src/surfer/fold/audit.js`; see [The Evidence](/the-evidence)).

## The amendment the implementation earned

The wiki's [Experience Engine](/the-experience-engine) framed the Given/Meant boundary as *segregation*: keep interpretation out of the record. The reader found a better rule. Reader-inferred edges — *this contradicts that*, *this connects to that* — **do** reach the graph, promoted as real `CON` edges that **carry their enactor provenance with them** (`src/enactor/connect/promote.js`, `src/surfer/fold/significance.js`). The attention field moves; the witnessed record is byte-unchanged. The firewall was never "keep inferences off the graph." It is **"keep them distinguishable on the graph."** Impact without laundering.

## Search is the door between the doors

The most important consequence: an interpretation the system is uncertain about can be *converted* into a witness by going and looking. A search takes the engine's own guess (reafference) and fetches an external page that either corroborates it or does not (exafference). *The grounding gap is the query* — the unresolved span becomes the question to the world (`docs/web-search.md`). This is why the reader can hold a belief honestly and still improve it: the two doors are not a wall, they are a *turnstile* with a measured toll. See [Going and Looking](/going-and-looking).

---

In **EO (E.O.)**, an **emanon** (/ˈɛm.ə.nɒn/, EM-uh-non) is one of three entity types — alongside **protogons** and **holons** — that describe how phenomena manifest in the framework's 27-position capacity ground. Emanons are **ground-dominant** configurations: phenomena whose contextual or ambient character is strong relative to their figure (distinct identity) and pattern (relational structure) aspects. They are characterized by **multiplicative infinity (∞⤫)**, the tendency to proliferate discretely when subjected to direct examination.

The term was coined to replace ordinary-language words like "thing" or "entity," which carry assumptions of bounded identity that emanons structurally lack.

---

## Etymology

**Emanon** (/ˈɛm.ə.nɒn/, EM-uh-non) is a portmanteau drawing on three roots:

- **Emanation** (Latin *emanare*, "to flow forth") — capturing the sense of phenomena that issue from relational conditions rather than standing as independent objects.
- **ān on** (Old English, "into one, in one, at once") — pointing to the convergence of multiple tensions into a momentary form.
- **Anonymous** (Greek *anōnymos*, "without a name") — encoding the structural elusiveness of emanonic phenomena: the act of naming them alters the thing named.

The word is both singular and plural (*one emanon, many emanon*), following the pattern of English mass nouns like *data*, *fish*, and *wisdom*. This grammatical choice reflects a foundational claim: emanon cannot be cleanly individuated from the relational networks out of which they arise.

# Holon

In **EO (E.O.)**, a **holon **(ˈhoʊ.lɒn/ [HOH-lon]) is one of three entity types — alongside **emanon** and **protogons** — that describe how phenomena manifest in the framework's 27-position capacity ground. Holons are **pattern-dominant** configurations: phenomena whose recursive relational process is the most active, defining aspect — the mechanism that binds figure (distinct identity) and ground (contextual substrate) into mutual reinforcement rather than the state of balance itself. They are characterized by **recursive infinity (∞↻)**, the capacity for self-reference to depth — the ability to sustain themselves through their own operation.

Where emanon are "too vague" and protogons are "too unstable," holons are "too rigid." Their characteristic problem is that they won't adapt. This rigidity is not inherent to the concept but the pathological form of its strength: the same mutual reinforcement that makes a holon self-maintaining can also make it self-enclosing.

---

## Etymology and Prior Usage

**Holon** (from Greek *ὅλον*, *holon*, "whole," neuter of *ὅλος*, *holos*, "entire") was coined by Arthur Koestler in *The Ghost in the Machine* (1967) to name entities that are simultaneously wholes in their own right and parts of larger wholes. Koestler's insight was that natural and social systems are neither reducible to their components nor describable only as totalities; they are organized in nested hierarchies — which he termed **holarchies** — where every level functions both as an autonomous unit and as a constituent of the level above it.

# Definitions

*A working glossary of EO's terms. It is deliberately thin: each entry gives the short form and points to the article that owns the term. By the wiki's own account of [definition](/identity-and-definition), a definition is only as authoritative as its giver, so every entry names its giver. Where an article and this page disagree, the article wins. The older glossary in the [EO Handbook](/eo-handbook) (Appendix G) predates several reconciliations; where they differ, this page follows the current articles.*

---

## The framework

**EO.** Existential, Emergent, and Experiential Ontology. The three expansions are interchangeable by design and are not to be flattened into one. See [Experiential Ontology](/emergent-ontology-eo).

**Capacity ground.** EO's three-axis, 27-cell phase space (3 × 3 × 3). Its axes are Mode, Domain, and Object. See [The Three Dimensions of EO](/the-three-dimensions-of-eo) and [The EO Phase Space Cube](/the-eo-phase-space-cube).

**Mode** (Identity). The axis of directionality: Differentiating, Relating, Generating. *What is this becoming?*

**Domain** (Space). The axis of arena: Existence, Structure, Significance (called Interpretation in some articles). *Where does this occur?*

**Object** (Time). The axis of target: Ground, Figure, Pattern. Not clock-time but the temporal character of what is acted on. *What kind of thing is being acted on?* See [The Three Faces of EO](/the-three-faces-of-emergent-ontology).

**Face.** A 3 × 3 projection of the 27-cell structure, made by crossing two axes. There are three: the **Act face** (Mode × Domain: the nine operators, *what are you doing*), the **Site face** (Domain × Object: nine terrains, *where are you*), and the **Stance** or **Resolution face** (Mode × Object: nine stances, *how are you holding it*). Each shows what the others hide.

**Ground / Figure / Pattern (GFP).** The three-role structure found inside every axis: ground is the enabling condition, figure is the differentiated element, pattern is the stabilizing integration. A second-order observation about the axes, not what generates them. See [Ground / Figure / Pattern](/ground-figure-pattern).

**Triadic Minimum.** The principle that three elements, not two, are the smallest structure that sustains stable differentiation and transformation. See [The Triadic Minimum](/the-triadic-minimum).

**Khora.** The unnameable generative ground prior to all structure (Plato's "third kind" in the *Timaeus*). EO acknowledges it and does not claim to formalize it. See [The Khora, The Substate, and the 10,000 Things](/the-khora-the-substate-and-the-10000-things).

**Substrate.** EO's formalized structure: the helical morphospace of 27 transformation types with its dependency ordering. Co-emergent with the Khora, not a higher or lower level of reality.

---

## The nine operators

Atomic kinds of change, claimed to suffice to describe any transformation. Best read as **capacities** a system becomes able to do, not steps it executes. See [The Nine Operators](/the-nine-operators).

| Operator | Glyph | Triad | Role | Capacity |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **NUL** | ∅ | Existence | Ground | Not transform: the identity function on state. See [NUL](/nul). |
| **SIG** | ○ | Existence | Figure | Register an appearance: attention without enduring structure. See [SIG](/sig). |
| **INS** | ● | Existence | Pattern | Create a concrete instance: that a thing *is*, not what it is. See [INS](/ins). |

title: /de7d8411-f4ed-4cc1-ad77-1b701ec8f6a7/t3
text: ꩜ Is there a better spiral glyph than this?

title: /de7d8411-f4ed-4cc1-ad77-1b701ec8f6a7/t3/Bash
/de7d8411-f4ed-4cc1-ad77-1b701ec8f6a7/t3
text:
Probably not, if it has to render everywhere. I haven't verified font coverage on your machine, so the points below come from general knowledge of Unicode.

**What ꩜ is:** U+AA5C, CHAM PUNCTUATION SPIRAL. It's the only character in Unicode that is literally named a spiral, and the shape is good. Its weakness is that it sits in the Cham block, so many phones, Windows setups and web fonts have no glyph for it and show a blank box. It's also a punctuation mark in another script, so screen readers and search treat it as Cham text.

**Alternatives:**

| Glyph | Codepoint | Verdict |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 🌀 | U+1F300 | Renders on nearly everything, but it's a color emoji. It reads as "cyclone" or "dizzy," and you can't theme it. |
| 🐚 | U+1F41A | A real spiral shell, which fits a Fibonacci or growth reading, but it's an emoji and a literal seashell. |
| @ | U+0040 | A spiral in most fonts and everywhere available, but it means "at." |
| ↻ ⟳ ⥀ | U+21BB, U+27F3, U+2940 | Widely supported, but these are loops, not spirals. They suit recursion more than ascent. |

**My recommendation:** use a small inline SVG, a logarithmic spiral stroked with `currentColor`. It looks the same on every device, follows light and dark mode, and needs no font. The wiki already renders HTML, and the same SVG works as a favicon or nav mark. Keep ꩜ in the text as the fallback when you want a plain character.

One thing to check against the wiki: the operator glyph set already uses ○ ● ⊛ and others, and a spiral mark shouldn't be confused with them. ꩜ doesn't collide with any of them, and I found no existing use of ꩜ in the wiki.

If this is for the wiki's spiral article, tell me where it will appear (title, favicon, inline). I can draft the SVG, or swap the glyph in if you've decided.

title: /de7d8411-f4ed-4cc1-ad77-1b701ec8f6a7/t4
text: What about a circle inside of a circle?

title: /de7d8411-f4ed-4cc1-ad77-1b701ec8f6a7/t4
text:
A circle inside a circle is a better choice for font support. It's a weaker choice for what the glyph means in EO.

**Support:** these sit in the Geometric Shapes and Math Operators blocks, which most system fonts cover, so you avoid the blank-box problem of ꩜.

| Glyph | Codepoint | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ◎ | U+25CE | Bullseye. Two clean rings and the most legible at small sizes. |
| ⊚ | U+229A | Circled ring operator. The same shape, but it reads as a math operator. |
| ⊙ | U+2299 | Circled dot. It's a dot in a ring, not two rings, and it doubles as the astronomical Sun. |
| ◉ | U+25C9 | Fisheye. A solid dot in a ring. |

**Three problems with it for EO:**

1. **◉ collides with the operator set.** The wiki uses ○ for SIG and ● for INS. A ring around a dot reads as SIG containing INS, which is a claim you didn't intend. ◎ is safer, but it still sits next to those two.
2. **It's close to REC.** REC is ⊛, also a circled glyph. At small sizes ⊙, ⊚ and ⊛ blur together, and REC is the recursion operator, so a spiral mark that looks like it invites confusion.
3. **Concentric circles aren't a spiral.** Rings share a center and each is closed, so there's no turning and no ascent. The Spiral's point is that each pass returns to the same place at a new level. A bullseye also reads as a target, which EO already uses for [targeting](/scope).

**Recommendation:** if you want a circle in a circle, use **◎** and skip ◉. It works as a plain-text mark where an SVG isn't practical. For the Spiral itself, I'd still use the inline SVG. A spiral that opens outward keeps the sense of passes at new levels, which concentric rings lose.

If you want a mark that is neither a spiral nor an operator lookalike, I can try both in a quick specimen sheet at small sizes so you can compare them.

title: /de7d8411-f4ed-4cc1-ad77-1b701ec8f6a7/t5
text: U+229A I think this is the way to go right? For recursion

title: /de7d8411-f4ed-4cc1-ad77-1b701ec8f6a7/t5
text:
Only partly. Recursion already has a glyph in EO: REC is **⊛** (U+229B), which the wiki canonicalized to the shipped algebra. ⊚ is U+229A, the character right before it in the same block. Used for recursion, it would sit beside REC in two ways:

- **It looks like REC.** ⊚ and ⊛ are both circled marks, and at body-text size the ring and the asterisk blur together. People will read them as the same symbol or as a typo.
- **It doubles up the meaning.** If ⊚ also means recursion, a reader can't tell whether it means the REC operator or something else.

So the answer depends on what ⊚ would stand for:

- **If it marks the Spiral as a whole** (the repeated passes through the helix, each at a new level), ⊚ is defensible. That is a different thing from REC, which is one operator, the Significance-triad capacity to restructure the frame. A ring-in-a-ring also hints at the same center revisited. If you do this, say in the wiki that ⊚ is the Spiral and not an operator. I'd add it to [Definitions](/definitions) under the framework section so it can't be mistaken for REC.
- **If it means recursion in general,** don't. Use ⊛ and keep one glyph per idea.

The earlier caveat about ⊚ still applies. It isn't a spiral, because concentric rings have no turning and no ascent, so it can only point at the Spiral's return-to-center. If that's enough for you, ⊚ works.

I can add ⊚ to the Definitions page as the Spiral's mark, with a note that it is not REC. Do you want that?

title: /de7d8411-f4ed-4cc1-ad77-1b701ec8f6a7/t6
text: Then maybe we need the circle with the arrow

title: /de7d8411-f4ed-4cc1-ad77-1b701ec8f6a7/t6
text:
A circle with an arrow is a reasonable idea, but EO already uses one: **↻** (U+21BB) is in the holon's mark, **∞↻**. The holons article defines it as recursive infinity, "the capacity for self-reference to depth." So ↻ already means recursion in this framework. It's on the [Definitions](/definitions) page too.

What that means for your options:

- **Use ↻ for recursion as a general idea:** it fits, and the wiki already backs it. It has a different job from REC (⊛), which is one operator restructuring the frame. ↻ is the loop-back-into-itself mark. That's two glyphs for two distinct ideas, which is fine.
- **Use ↻ for the Spiral:** this overloads it. A reader would take the mark as "holon" or "recursive depth," not "the repeated passes through the helix."
- **Pick a twin for the Spiral** (↺, ⟳, ⟲, ⥁): I'd avoid this. These look almost identical at body size and have no meaning that tells them apart, so nobody could read the difference.
- **Arrow vs. spiral:** the arrow gives direction and repetition, which ⊚ lacked. But a circle with an arrow still closes on itself, so it doesn't show each pass landing at a new level. It also suggests a procedure, and the wiki says the helix is a dependency of enablement and not a recipe you execute.

**My recommendation is to keep ↻ as it is and not mint a new mark for recursion.** For the Spiral, use ⊚ (labeled as the Spiral, not an operator) or the inline SVG, and let the SVG carry the level-change that glyphs can't.

If you want to change what ↻ means in the wiki, that touches the holon and entity-type articles, and I'd want to read them before touching anything.

text: Yeah, I don't really care about the whole odd one. I just think that the* is weird and really what we wanted to note is ascending to a higher level like we're finding. When we're falsifying something, we get to the end and we find that something's not grounded. We go backwards, but what we're doing is we are recording the history of what we did. So we're going backwards, but we retain the process of getting there which means that we're going up a level

title: /de7d8411-f4ed-4cc1-ad77-1b701ec8f6a7/t7
text:
That reading of REC matches how the wiki already describes it. A reframe in [Going and Looking](/going-and-looking) flags earlier answers as stale and re-checks them. Retraction is a SEG event, never an erasure, and the log only grows. You step back, but the way you got there is kept, so the earlier run becomes content at the new level. That is the ascent. ⊛ doesn't show any of it.

This revises what I said earlier. I treated the Spiral and REC as separate things, but if REC is "return with the trail kept, one level up," the spiral is the right picture for REC itself.

There is a constraint, though. REC's glyph isn't only wiki decoration. The wiki canonicalized the glyph set to the shipped algebra, and [EOT](/eot) recovers operators from punctuation, so REC has to be one real Unicode character. An SVG can't do that job, and neither can anything drawn per page. That narrows the choices:

| Glyph | Codepoint | What it shows | Problem |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ꩜ | U+AA5C | A literal spiral: return at a new level | Poor font coverage (the blank-box problem) |
| ↰ | U+21B0 | Heading up while the tip points back, close to "backtrack but ascend" | An arrow, so it suggests a procedure, and it doesn't show the retained trail |
| ⤴ | U+2934 | Turn and rise | Shows on many platforms as a color emoji |

If I had to pick one, it's **↰**, as the only one that renders reliably and still carries both "back" and "up." ꩜ says more but would break wherever the font is missing, and that would be a parser-adjacent symbol failing silently.

Before changing REC's glyph, I'd want to count where ⊛ lives: the operator definitions in the reader, tests, vendored copies, and the wiki. That is a cross-repo change, so I'd confirm the scope with you before editing any sibling repo. I can run a read-only search for ⊛ across the repos and tell you how many places it appears.

Should I run that search, or do you want to settle the glyph first?

result: {"stdout":"### Practitioner Glyphs

The practitioner glyph system is **∅ ○ ● ｜ ⋈ △ ⊢ ⊨ ⊛** — one mark per operator, made authoritative in the implementation (`src/core/operators.js`) so every surface draws the same mark for a given act and a graph edge never disagrees with a legend chip. The marks read by domain column: Existence **∅ ○ ●**, Structure **｜ ⋈ △**, Interpretation **⊢ ⊨ ⊛**. Glyphs were selected for visual iconicity:

- **∅** (empty set) for NUL: the void as a well-defined mathematical object.
- **○** (open circle) for SIG: attention directed but not yet filled — a point of registration, something becoming salient against a ground, prior to any boundary being drawn around it.
- **●** (filled circle) for INS: the registration made concrete — a particular brought into being.
- **｜** (vertical bar, U+FF5C) for SEG: a boundary, a wall, a partition.
- **⋈** (bowtie/natural join) for CON: two things meeting at a point — borrowed from relational algebra's join symbol.
- **△** (triangle) for SYN: parts rising into an emergent whole.
- **⊢** (turnstile) for DEF: entailment — what follows given the terms; a definition asserted.
- **⊨** (double turnstile) for EVA: satisfaction — testing whether a structure models a formula.
- **⊛** (rightwards arrow with loop) for REC: output feeding back as input, the helix bending into a spiral.

**Superseded glyphs**, kept for reading older material: ⊡ (was SIG, now ○); △ (was INS — now SYN's mark, INS is ●); ⤫ (was CON, now ⋈); ∨ (was SYN, now △); ∿ (was DEF, now ⊢); ∥ (was EVA, now ⊨). The earlier set drifted from the implementation; the marks above are the ones the shipped reader draws.

text:
**The current canonical set** is **∅ ○ ● ｜ ⋈ △ ⊢ ⊨ ⊛**, from [Operator Naming](/operator-naming-in-emergent-ontology), which says it was made authoritative in the implementation (`src/core/operators.js`).

| Operator | NUL | SIG | INS | SEG | CON | SYN | DEF | EVA | REC |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Glyph | ∅ | ○ | ● | ｜ | ⋈ | △ | ⊢ | ⊨ | ⊛ |

**No operator ever had a circle inside a circle.** I searched the wiki, the historian's snapshots, the compendium, the handbook and the constitution. The wiki lists these superseded glyphs: ⊡ (was SIG), △ (was INS), ⤫ (was CON), ∨ (was SYN), ∿ (was DEF) and ∥ (was EVA). The closest is ⊡, a square with a dot in it, so you may be remembering that one. If you remember a ring-in-ring from somewhere specific, it isn't in anything I could read.

**The REC rationale doesn't match the glyph.** The wiki justifies ⊛ as a "rightwards arrow with loop" meaning output feeding back as input, a helix bending into a spiral. But U+229B is a circled asterisk, not an arrow with a loop. The text describes a different character. I can't confirm which, but ↬ (U+21AC, "rightwards arrow with loop") appears in penelope's glyph inventory and fits that description. That supports your sense that the asterisk is odd. The glyph and its stated reason never agreed.

I haven't changed anything yet. The edit I'd propose for the wiki:

- Replace ⊛ with **⊚** across the articles (about 22 files) and in the site's sigil table in `index.html`, which uses ⊛ in four places.
- Rewrite the REC rationale to your argument: retracing while keeping the trail puts the earlier run inside a new frame.
- Add "⊛ (was REC, now ⊚)" to the superseded list.

Two warnings. The wiki would then disagree with `src/core/operators.js`, which it cites as authoritative, until the reader is changed too. Also, the decal forms ⊛−, ⊛+ and ⊛\* in khora's `grain-glyphs.html` would become ⊚−, ⊚+ and ⊚\*, so the asterisk survives as the Pattern decal.

Should I make the wiki edit and push it, or hold until the reader's glyph changes? I'd leave the compendium and historian copies alone, since they're pinned records.

I sent you a specimen sheet. It shows the current ⊛ and five candidates at 12, 16, 24 and 48px, and each one set in line with the other eight operators. I haven't looked at the render myself, so I can't say how they look on your screen.

**Candidates for a ring with a solid dot inside:**

| Glyph | Codepoint | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ⊙ | U+2299 | Circled dot. Same block as ⊛, one slot away. The dot is small, so it should stay clear of ●. It is also the astronomical Sun and the "dot product," which only matter in math contexts. |
| ◉ | U+25C9 | Fisheye. Same block as ○ and ●, so it reads as a family: ○ ● ◉. The dot is big, so at small sizes it may blur into ●. |
| ⦿ | U+29BF | Circled bullet. A heavier dot, but weaker font coverage. |

**My pick is ⊙**, mainly because of the small dot. That keeps REC from reading as a fuzzy INS. It also sits in the operator block with ⋈ ⊢ ⊨, like ⊛ did. ◉ is the better fit if it turns out to look fine at 12 to 16px, because it belongs with ○ and ●. The specimen is the quickest way to tell.

I haven't edited anything yet. Pick ⊙, ◉ or ⦿ and I'll make the wiki edit I described: swap the glyph in the articles and the site's sigil table, rewrite the REC rationale around retraced-run-kept-inside-a-new-frame, and add "⊛ (was REC)" to the superseded list. I'll also hold the push until you say whether the reader's `operators.js` is changing in step.

text:
REC's glyph is now ◉ in the wiki edit, but it is committed locally as `60c5513` and **not pushed**. The branch is one commit ahead of `origin/main`, and the full-export build still counts 80 articles.

What changed, 25 files:
- **Glyph swap:** ⊛ → ◉ throughout the articles, 62 occurrences. The decal forms follow along (◉−, ◉+, ◉\*), and the site's sigil table and linker in `index.html` are updated.
- **REC rationale:** the old text said "rightwards arrow with loop," which described a different character. It now gives your argument. A retraced run is kept as instantiated record (●), inside a new frame that is registered but not yet filled in (○). It is built from the SIG and INS marks on purpose.
- **Handbook:** the REC row in the codepoint table now reads U+25C9 with that visual logic. It used to say "Circled asterisk."
- **Superseded list:** ⊛ is recorded as REC's former glyph. The Definitions page also carries a note on it.

Why I held the push: the wiki cites `src/core/operators.js` as the authority for the glyph set, and that file still draws ⊛. If I push now, the wiki contradicts the code it points to. If you're changing the reader in step, say so and I'll push. The pinned copies in `eo-compendium` and `eo-historian` stay untouched, since they're records. On the khora side, `native/docs/grain-glyphs.html` is the only live file that shows ⊛ (including ⊛−, ⊛+, ⊛\*). I haven't edited it, because that's a sibling repo.

Two small things to know:
- **Existing ◉ elsewhere:** `articles/experiment/phaseposts.md` already uses ◉ for "Gravity well." The site's sigil linker could in principle read that as REC, but experiments run sandboxed, so it shouldn't be affected. I haven't checked it in a browser.
- **Small-size legibility:** whether the ring reads clearly against ● at 12 to 16px is for you to judge from the specimen sheet I sent earlier.

Push the wiki now, or wait until the reader's glyph is changed too?

def files(repo,exclude=()):
    out=subprocess.run(['rg','-l','⊛',repo,'-g','!node_modules','-g','!*.json','-g','!*.jsonl'],capture_output=True,text=True).stdout.split()
    return [f for f in out if not any(e in f for e in exclude)]

for repo in ['eodb','eopm','municipal-db','caselink-scraper']:

        lines=open(f,encoding='utf-8').read().split('\n')

            i+=1
        open(f,'w',encoding='utf-8').write('\n'.join(out))
        touched.setdefault(repo,[]).append(f)

text:
REC is now ◉ in the repos that hold the glyph, as local commits. **Nothing is pushed.** I'm waiting on you for the pushes.

**What changed, by repo**

| Repo | Commit | What |
| --- | --- | --- |
| eo-wiki | `60c5513` | 25 files: articles, the site's sigil table, the REC rationale, the handbook table, the superseded list |
| khora (scores-patch-points) | `f1f0898` | Glyph table, 27-cell docs page, surface comment, sample surface |
| khora | `87dd387` | `operatorOfGlyph`: one lookup that reads ⊛ and ↬ as REC, plus a test (5/5 pass) |
| penelope | branch `glyph-rec-circled-dot`, `40dc851` | `GLYPH`/`MARK`, legend, zones, and a `GL-TP-05` entry in `GLAUCA-EOT.md` |
| eodb, eopm, municipal-db, caselink-scraper | `474977d`, `c91bc11`, `13e5a9e`, `bc1605f` | Code and docs. eodb and eopm tests pass |
| NPJ | `7269423` | 7 files, on the `fast-boot-reliable-uploads` branch |

**Ingesting prior versions:** before this, no code in the scores-patch-points repos read a glyph back to an operator, so nothing breaks on old data. The glyph only appears in output tables. Records already written keep ⊛ (penelope's keep ↬). `operatorOfGlyph` in khora is the one place that now resolves all three marks. △ is deliberately not aliased, because it used to be INS and is now SYN.

**Things you should know**
- **I made one mistake and fixed it.** I briefly staged someone's uncommitted `package.json` edit into a khora commit. I undid that, so `87dd387` holds only my files and their edit is still uncommitted. It also means the new khora test isn't in `npm test` yet.
- **Penelope's font law is not met.** ◉ is carried by only Menlo and DejaVu Sans Mono among its target fonts, the same as ↬ was. `GL-TP-04` calls for a safe stand-in, but that mechanism isn't in this trimmed repo, so MARK prints ◉ raw. The entry says so and leaves REC's safe stand-in open.
- **Penelope's cloth isn't re-woven.** `--stamp` refuses at `HEAD`, and the checker already had 98 failures before my change. Mine adds 20, all of the form "cloth still prints ↬". They clear when someone re-weaves after the in-progress spec lands.
- **Three NPJ files are edited but uncommitted:** `Documents.jsx`, `Newsroom.jsx` and `ArticleRead.jsx`, which had others' work in progress.
- **I changed some neighbouring ◉ bullets to ◆:** khora's inspector heading, municipal-db's "x-ray" link and NPJ's "Preview" toggle, so they don't read as REC.

**Not touched**
- **Vendored and snapshot copies still show ⊛:** holodeck's vendored copy, ohs-custody, ethos and the untracked `ab` copy. The fix belongs upstream in `bare-metal-eo-matrix-app`, then re-vendor.
- **Pinned records:** the compendium and the historian.
- **Frozen repos and clones:** eochat, eoWebLLM, eochatX, eoreader6, the `-latest`/`-legacy` and `eoreader7-*` clones.
- **The tokenizer file:** `gemma2-tokenizer.json` has ⊛ as a vocabulary token.
- **An older drift I found but didn't fix:** the app family still uses ⤫ for CON, where the wiki canon is ⋈.

Which pushes do you want? I'd start with khora and the wiki, and push penelope's branch separately so it doesn't land on top of its uncommitted work. The wiki needs the `clovenbradshaw-ctrl` token again. I can also clone the upstream `bare-metal-eo-matrix-app` template, update it, and re-vendor holodeck.

# 09 — Source Code

Collected source files, licences and substantive upstream documentation from
major open-source projects. This file is repo-authored (an index, not a
prior); everything else in this section except `VETTING.md` is collected
upstream material.

## Two tiers

**Audited tier** — projects selected because their security posture is
*externally documented*: a published third-party audit, machine-checked
formal verification, or a continuous audit process. Fetched by
`scripts/fetch-audited-code.mjs` at **pinned commits**: the branch head is
resolved to a SHA before fetching, every file's sha256 is recorded in
`manifests/audited-code-manifest.json`, and `scripts/vet-source-code.mjs`
re-verifies the bytes on disk against those checksums on every run. Each
directory carries a `PROVENANCE.md` with the pinned commit, the security
review record with citations, per-file checksums, and any short collected
documents (licences, security policies) folded in rather than dropped.

REC (recontextualize) is drawn **◉** (U+25C9, ring around a filled circle), not ⊛ (U+229B). The user's reasoning: going back after a falsification keeps the trail, so it is a move up a level. Solid centre = ● (INS, the retraced run kept as record); open ring = ○ (SIG, a new layer registered but not yet filled in). Superseded marks: ⊛ (the wiki's old mark; its stated rationale "arrow with loop" never matched a circled asterisk) and ↬ (penelope's tapestry mark). Canon chain: eo-wiki → khora `grounding-glyphs.mjs` (declares it follows the wiki) → vendored copies.

**Why:** the user found the asterisk odd; wanted REC to read as ascent that retains history. Said scores-patch-points repos matter most, and that anything ingesting prior versions must be updated.

- BRANCHES, not main (review first): penelope `glyph-rec-circled-dot`, NPJ `glyph-rec-circled-dot`

**Method that mattered:** khora main, penelope main and the-fold carry the user's OWN unpushed commits, and several repos have uncommitted WIP in the same files. Never push a branch that contains them; replay my commits onto `origin/<branch>` in a temp worktree and push that. For dirty files stage only my lines (`git hash-object -w` of HEAD-with-substitution + `git update-index --cacheinfo`). Local khora/NPJ branches still hold duplicate local copies of the pushed commits; a `git pull --rebase` drops them.

**Still owed:**
- penelope: the tapestry cloth is not re-woven (`node gym/check-tapestry.mjs --stamp` refuses at HEAD: COVER; the in-progress spec has to land first); checker already had ~98 findings, my change adds ~12-20 until re-woven. ◉ is native only to Menlo + DejaVu in the target monospace fonts, so it breaks GL-TP-04 like ↬ did; REC needs a safe stand-in once the safe profile exists (not implemented in this trimmed repo). text:
REC's glyph is now ◉ across the repos that carry it. Everything is pushed except penelope and NPJ, which went up as branches (reasons below).

**Pushed to `main`**
- **eo-wiki:** `60c5513`, live now. The full export has 55 lines with ◉, and the only 2 with ⊛ are the supersession notes.
- **khora:** `e52a5a8` on `main` and `8463738` on `fold/handlers`. It now has `operatorOfGlyph`, which reads ⊛ and ↬ as REC, for anything ingesting older records. The tests pass at the remote's tip.
- **eodb, eopm, municipal-db, caselink-scraper:** `474977d`, `c91bc11`, `13e5a9e`, `bc1605f`.
- **Upstream template `bare-metal-eo-matrix-app`:** `db7b440`.
- **holodeck:** `d929a2e`. The vendored files were re-copied byte-identical from khora and the template, the local shim was edited directly, and it's logged in `VENDORING.md`. Its tests pass.
- **ohs-custody:** `2ec2010`. Two vendored files were hand-synced and logged in `docs/holodeck/VENDOR.md`.

**Pushed as branches, not `main`**
- **penelope, `glyph-rec-circled-dot`:** its tapestry check gains failures until the cloth is re-woven, and I can't re-weave without the in-progress spec.
- **NPJ, `glyph-rec-circled-dot`:** this repo is on a feature branch with other people's work, and the app may deploy from `main`.

**How I avoided publishing your own work.** Khora `main`, penelope `main` and `the-fold` hold your unpushed commits, and several repos have uncommitted edits in the same files. I rebuilt my commits on each remote's tip rather than pushing your branches. For the files with work in progress (three NPJ files and holodeck's `index.html`), I committed only my glyph lines. I did stage your `package.json` into a khora commit once by mistake, then undid it. Your local khora and NPJ branches still hold duplicate copies of my commits, and a `git pull --rebase` drops them.

**Left alone on purpose**
- **`ethos/09-source-code`:** a checksummed corpus of upstream code, not our documentation.
- **Pinned and frozen copies:** the compendium, the historian, the frozen legacy repos and the `-latest`/`-legacy`/`eoreader7-*` clones.
- **Legacy `clovenbradshaw-ctrl/holodeck` line:** not touched.
- **`the-fold`:** it carries no glyph.

**Still open**
- **Penelope's cloth:** re-weave with `node gym/check-tapestry.mjs --stamp` once your spec lands. ◉ is native only to Menlo and DejaVu among its target fonts, so it breaks `GL-TP-04` as ↬ did, and REC still needs a safe stand-in. The `GL-TP-05` entry in `GLAUCA-EOT.md` records both points.
- **Khora's test script:** it needs the new glyph test added once your `package.json` edit is committed.
- **CON glyph drift:** the app family and holodeck's `index.html` still use ⤫ for CON, where the wiki canon is ⋈.
- **Template tests:** 5 date-formula tests fail in the template with or without my change.

input: {"command":"cd /Users/mlacy/Documents/3.0/khora/native/docs && wc -l THE-HOLOGRAPH.md && sed -n 1,120p THE-HOLOGRAPH.md | cut -c1-400","description":"Read the first part of THE-HOLOGRAPH.md"}
result: {"stdout":"     522 THE-HOLOGRAPH.md
# The Holograph

**Standing: nomination.** This document names what the instrument does when
it hands a reading to a consumer, gives it a lineage, and says what it might
unlock. It is checkable against the code and the record, and both win any
disagreement with it. Written 2026-09-07, the day the idea was named, with
its first measurements still running (the pending ones are marked).

## 1. The claim

The record is the object. What any consumer is handed — the mouth, a reader,
a person at the page — is not the object but a small pattern computed from
it: a few addressed holons, each standing in for the material it was
computed from, from which any part of the whole can be re-expanded by the
record. Never by the consumer.

Three properties make that a holograph rather than a summary:

1. **Every part points at the whole.** Each line the record produces carries
   an address into the record — a byte range in a source, a turn, a note's
   witnesses — and the record can expand that address to the bytes, the
   claims around them, the referent's whole neighbourhood. The line is small;
   what it refers to is not. This is the standing rule about holonic objects
   in slots ("one address refers losslessly to a whole universe") applied to
   what is handed, not only to what is stored.
2. **Abstraction compresses.** A Lens line (a claim with its standing) stands
   in for the sentence it was read from. A Paradigm line (an act that recurs
   between two referents) stands in for every occurrence of it. An
   Atmosphere line (where the conversation stands) stands in for the run of
   exchanges it was computed over. So the more resolution a consumer is
   handed, the less it should need — the level ladder is a compression
   ladder, and if it does not compress, the abstraction failed, not the
   consumer.
3. **The consumer never gets the addresses.** A model handed an address will
   write one, and a written address is a fabrication order. The pattern
   reaches the mouth with every address struck (one wall at the mouth's
   door, `firewall.js::mouthFacing`); the record keeps them all and attaches
   them to the answer afterwards, mechanically (`cite.js`). Re-expansion is a
   door the record opens (`/reopen`, the quote door, the record check), not
   a thing the mouth does.

The consequence the whole design bets on: the size of what the mouth sees
becomes independent of the size of the material. A novel or a shelf of them
costs the same few hundred tokens per turn, because the reading happened
once, at admission, by structure, and a turn is a query over it cut where
widening stops making a difference.

## 2. What it is not

It is not retrieval-augmented generation. RAG hands a model raw chunks chosen
by string similarity and lets the model read them. The holograph hands
computed readings, resolved by referent identity, cut by a measured window,
with the addresses held back. The model reads nothing; it voices.

It is not a summary written by a model. The one place a model used to read
the discourse whole — the summary-refresh call that wrote the fold's topic,
flow and entities — is exactly what the Atmosphere block replaces with a
reading computed from referent sets per exchange. A paraphrase is the thing
the old PAST DISCOURSE block warned the model not to mine; a reading has no
such warning to give.

It is not lossy compression of tokens. Every line is exact and re-expandable
to bytes. What is lost is only what was never in the reading — and that is a
fact about the reader, disclosed on the record, not a property of the
pattern.

## 3. Prior art

The name is a metaphor with a real ancestry, and several technical lineages
converge on the shape.

**Optics and the brain.** Gabor's holography (1948) records an interference
pattern from which the whole image is reconstructed, and any fragment of the
plate reconstructs the whole at … [3516 more chars at the transcript address]

text:
**Short answer: we don't know it yet.** I found no document, test or measurement that classifies a word's part of speech from how it affects the holographic field. [`THE-HOLOGRAPH.md`](../khora/native/docs/THE-HOLOGRAPH.md) says nothing about word classes. It is about what a consumer is handed. The nearest "field" in the code is the `Field` in `khora/native/the-fold/relative.js`, a sparse-code memory with recall and a measured null band. I'm assuming that's what you mean by the field.

What the repos do hold is adjacent, and some of it is measured:

**1. Part of speech is currently conventional.** `khora/native/adapters/text/english-parser.js` uses an averaged-perceptron tagger over the word and its neighbours, trained on UD_English-EWT. The house cites 74% held-out recall for it. Nothing in it comes from field behaviour.

**2. Class is an input to the cue learner, and measured as necessary.** `morph-cues.js` learns tense, case and number from co-occurrence, each cue conditioned on the word class. Its header lists three measured failures without that conditioning:
- Latin case endings fired on 99.8% of finite verbs.
- A tense marked by the absence of an auxiliary had no cue that could carry it.
- The class-alone cue fired on every token of its class.

**3. Company can place a referent's kind, but not part of speech.** `khora/native/organs/kind-standing.js` reads what kind of thing a referent is from the single token before and after each mention. Its header says it uses no part of speech, no semantic label and no word list, and it uses counts rather than sets. A presence/absence PMI gate "did not separate anything." Two of the null models it tried were refuted before the third worked.

**4. Nominal grain by elimination.** `khora/native/adapters/text/existence-grain.js` splits Entity, Kind and Void by what a form refuses: determiners, a settled prior, lowercase mid-line, burstiness against a shuffle. It was measured on *Doctor Faustus*, *Henry IV Part 1* and *Antigone*.
- The article cue is register-particular. Attic prose puts the article on names, while tragic verse and English don't.
- The burstiness "kill" removed 9 real names in two English plays and 9 in *Antigone*, so it's reported but never licensed.
- The strongest cue is orthographic (capitalisation), which is the least universal. It has never been run on a caseless script.

**5. Function words behave differently in the field, which is the closest hint.** In `khora/native/memory/activation.js`, short function words were left out of the document-frequency table. "The" then scored as maximally rare, filler trigrams became top keys, the sparse code stopped being sparse, and every frame recalled every previous one. The same comment says a length cutoff can't separate function words from short content words ("any", "did" vs "ice", "sun"). It points to a Zipf-derived closed-class test, `material.js::functionWordSet`, that needs a retrieval-quality golden to validate.

So closed-class words do have a distinctive field signature: extreme frequency and flooding when unhandled. Nothing yet extends that to nouns, verbs or adjectives.

**What I'd propose, since the evidence stops there:** a pre-registered test on the gold-tagged treebank you already hold.
- **Method:** compute each word's field footprint (document frequency, burstiness, activation reach, neighbour company) and predict coarse part of speech on a held-out tenth.
- **Controls:** a frequency-only baseline and the same features on word-shuffled text, run against the perceptron's number.
- **Likely outcome:** the closed-class split should come out well. A noun/verb/adjective split is the open question. I haven't run anything, and I'd state the thresholds before running.

Want me to write that pre-registration, or are you thinking of a different mechanism than what I assumed?
